tldr: This thread is a reading list of LLM research grouped by shared wording, not one event. From Oct 27 it ran from continual learning and pruning through Anthropic's Nov 2 provable-inference update and knowledge editing to Nov 10-12 studies questioning what eval scores measure: rater drift, name-anchored recall and corrupted-input shortcuts.
whats_new: Nov 13: a black-box uncertainty method uses an ensemble of ensembles to split prompt ambiguity from genuine knowledge gaps without the compute cost of Bayesian or deep-ensemble approaches.
why_it_matters: Most items are single unreplicated preprints, but the latest run touches production reliability: scores can survive name removal or shuffled inputs, and black-box uncertainty is the signal an API-only deployment has for deciding when to abstain or escalate.

beats.headline: Keeping models current: compatibility-aware replay and RL-driven self-learning
beats.summary: Two papers on acquiring new knowledge without losing old capabilities.

beats.headline: Efficiency work: extreme-sparsity pruning and an early-stopping audit for reasoning models
beats.summary: A text-to-SQL architecture survey lands the same day.

beats.headline: Anthropic reports progress on zkSNARK-based provable inference
beats.summary: The thread's only lab-published item: cryptographic proofs applied to LLM inference.

beats.headline: Updating what models know: answerability drift, multimodal unlearning and lifelong knowledge editing
beats.summary: Also here: an LLM choosing federated aggregation rules without training.

beats.headline: Judgment under scrutiny: rising rater standards on Chatbot Arena, framing effects and personality benchmarks
beats.summary: These days also bring an LLM AutoML searcher, physics-guided fault diagnosis, a training-simulation benchmark and a cognitive account of learning by thinking.

beats.headline: What do scores measure? ShadowBench and a corrupted-input study probe shortcuts behind passing evals
beats.summary: One tests recall without explicit entity names; the other asks whether LLMs pass NLI on noun-stripped or shuffled inputs.

beats.headline: Black-box uncertainty quantification separates prompt ambiguity from knowledge gaps
beats.summary: An ensemble-of-ensembles method aimed at models reachable only through an API.

open_questions: Does the ensemble-of-ensembles method report how many model calls per prompt it needs, and how that compares with deep ensembles?
Do published unlearning or knowledge-editing methods still pass when probed without explicit entity names, as ShadowBench suggests they may not?
Does the corruption study find LLMs keep accuracy on shuffled or noun-stripped inputs, and does it attribute that to shortcuts or memorised test data?
Do Chatbot Arena or other human-preference leaderboards adjust rankings for the rater drift the Nov 10 study describes?
Does Anthropic publish proving cost or latency figures for zkSNARK-based provable inference?
Does the early-stopping audit identify a method that cuts reasoning tokens without lowering reliability?
take_for_builders: Add perturbed controls to your eval suite (paraphrased entity names, shuffled inputs), and before adopting black-box uncertainty for abstention, measure its extra call cost per request.
